correctness.rationale: For every d≥2, independent Dirichlet integration gives interior pair moment 2S/((d+1)(d+2)) and area-weighted boundary pair moment 2S/(d(d+1))−2||I−G||²/d². The outward-face-normal equilibrium forces each facet weight below 1/2. A Cauchy–Schwarz bound then gives ||I−G||²/S < (d−1)/(2(d+1)), and substitution proves the strict ratio. Explicit full-dimensional vertices with two near +e0 and d−1 near −e0 have exactly computed facet Gram determinants, and converge to this bound, proving optimality. For d≥4 the limiting ratio is below one; regular simplices have ratio (d+2)/d above one. The packaged checker passed 1204 supplementary comparisons; analytic proof, not finite testing, establishes all quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The exact general second-moment identities in Lotnikov are explicitly prior; the proposed addition is the sharp infimum (d+1)(d+2)/(2d²) over all nondegenerate d-simplices, proof that it is not attained, a full-dimensional extremizing family, and the dimension-four sign reversal within simplices. Tokmachev and Shen analyze distinct classes or first moments. The closest related archived result is a two-dimensional triangle moment gap rather than an all-dimensional sharp ratio. Direct source overlap was compared by implication, not titles; no known checked theorem subsumes the new sharp optimization. Historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The Zaporozhets–Tarasov boundary/interior mean-distance comparison is an active and difficult geometric-probability question, with dimension-dependent general failures. This result supplies a sharp, all-dimensional squared-distance ratio for an intrinsic and canonical infinite family, proves the infimum cannot occur inside shape space, constructs a sharp degeneration, and locates a previously unspecified failure of the squared comparison already among four-dimensional simplices. Its point is the natural optimal constant and geometric transition, not an arbitrary restricted numerical exercise.
